components.css: .ds-tiles { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 124px); gap: 8px; } .ds-tile { display: grid; gap: 2px; justify-items: start; padding: 12px; border-radius: 12px; border: 1px solid #e2e2de; background: #f7f7f5; color: #18191b; font: 14px/1.45 'Segoe UI Variable Text','Segoe UI',system-ui,sans-serif; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; transition: transform .25s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), border-color .2s, background .2s, box-shadow .25s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); } .ds-tile svg { width: 22px; height: 22px; margin-bottom: 8px; color: #5b5e63; transition: transform .45s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), color .2s; } .ds-tile:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); border-color: #d1d1cc; background: #fff; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(24,25,27,.06), 0 8px 24px -12px rgba(24,25,27,.18); } .ds-tile:hover svg { transform: scale(1.12) rotate(-6deg); color: #18191b; } .ds-tile:active { transform: translateY(0) scale(.98); } .ds-tile:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #18191b; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-tile-name { font-weight: 600; } .ds-tile-num { font-size: 12px; color: #5b5e63; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-tile-on { background: #f8e9b4; border-color: #d9b440; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #d9b440; } .ds-tile-on svg { color: #7a5b00; }

narrative.overview:
The AK820 itself carries the screen. Its own colorway (black case, light-ash alphas, dark-ash modifiers, mustard Esc, Enter and Space) is drawn large and central, and the rest of the app is a quiet light-ash workroom around it: white panels on an ash ground, ink type, one stroke of Lucide line icons. The interface borrows its only accent from the yellow keycaps, and spends it where the keycaps would: on what is selected and on the one action that sends changes to the keyboard.

Density is that of a settings tool, not a dashboard: a 248px sidebar, a stage with the board and its status row, then effect tiles and a controls panel. Depth is soft and ambient; the only dramatic shadow belongs to the physical board. Motion is purposeful: the board's legends and underglow take the current lighting colour and cross-fade when it changes, and the board lights up once when you connect or explore. The system refuses the dark gamer dashboard and the wall of flat tabs.
keyCharacteristics: The rendered keyboard is the hero on every lighting and key surface.
Ash neutrals, ink text, mustard as the single accent.
System UI face; mono only for hex and capture data.
Lucide line icons at one stroke weight (1.9).
Explicit Apply: changes are staged, the status row says so, mustard sends them.

rules.name: The Keycap Rule
rules.body: Mustard is used the way the yellow caps are: on the selected thing and the one primary action. A screen carries one mustard-filled button.

rules.name: The Board Owns Its Colours Rule
rules.body: Case, cap and knob colours live on the keyboard render only; UI chrome never borrows Case Black as a surface.

rules.name: The Native Face Rule
rules.body: No display face. Hierarchy comes from weight (400 / 600 / 650) and size, not from a second family.

rules.name: The One Object Rule
rules.body: Only the keyboard casts a deep shadow. UI surfaces stay at the panel shadow or flat.

dos: Do keep the keyboard render visible and central on lighting and key surfaces.
Do spend mustard only on selection and the single primary action (The Keycap Rule).
Do stage changes and state them ("Not sent yet") until the user presses Apply; keep Apply in the status row above the board.
Do use Lucide line icons at the shared 1.9 stroke, 16px in chrome, 22px on tiles.
Do ease every state change with cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1) and honour reduced-motion.
Do use mono only for hex, packets and shortcuts.
donts: Don't turn the app into a dark gamer dashboard or a wall of flat tabs.
Don't add a second accent hue; status colours report state and are never decoration.
Don't give UI surfaces the board's deep shadow or Case Black fill.
Don't apply lighting changes live; Apply is explicit.
